info.name: College of the Apocalypse
info.description: The College of the Apocalypse subclass for the Bard from Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024).
info.author: MonkeyDM

element.name: College of the Apocalypse
element.source: Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: Apocalypse Bards are masters at conjuring forth the ancient powers of eldritch gods, summoning forth their otherworldly might to wreak havoc on the mortal realm. All who hear their aberrant harmonies fear and revere them—they understand that with a single whisper, these Bards can cause the end of all things. Apocalypse Bards are often found on the front lines of battle, their music serving as a rallying cry for their allies and a death knell for their enemies. With each stanza they produce, a member of the College of the Apocalypse draws closer to the ultimate revelation of the horrors that lie beyond the veil. Many fear the day when they will finally succumb to the madness that gnaws within their mind.

As they progress in their studies, members of this college gain the ability to summon forth devastating powers with their music. They can call down swarms of pain, tear open rifts in reality, and unleash waves of madness upon their foes. They know the apocalypse is coming, for they are the ones bringing it.

element.name: Level 3: Eldritch Choir
element.source: Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: You understand how to use your bardic magic to conjure the power of the Great Ones. You learn two Eldritch Melodies of your choice, which are detailed under "Eldritch Melodies" below. To learn an Eldritch Melody, you must meet its prerequisite.

You can use a melody as an action, expending one use of your Bardic Inspiration. If a melody requires a saving throw, it uses your spell save DC. For a creature to become affected by one of your melodies, it must be able to hear you when you take the action. After you use a melody, you can't use that melody again until you finish a Short Rest or Long Rest.
Some Eldritch Melodies require Concentration and are marked as such.

Replacing and Gaining Eldritch Melodies. When you finish a Long Rest, you can delve into what lies beyond the veil, replacing one or more melodies you know with another one. Each time you attempt to replace a melody, make a DC 17 Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, you lose control over your mental journey into the void; you gain one Short-Term Madness, don't replace that melody, and you can't replace any other melodies until you finish a Long Rest.
When you reach Bard level 6 and 14, you learn one additional Eldritch Melody of your choice.

sheet.description: Use an Eldritch Melody as an action by expending 1 Bardic Inspiration (DC{{bard:spellcasting:dc}}; targets must hear you). Each melody can be used once per Short or Long Rest. When replacing melodies on a Long Rest, make a DC 17 Cha save per attempt or gain Short-Term Madness, fail to replace it, and stop replacing until next Long Rest.

element.name: Level 6: Knowledge from Beyond
element.source: Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: The maddening revelations that haunt your mind guide you through the treacherous void. You know Deep Speech. Additionally, whenever you make an Intelligence check that relates to the cosmos or the eldritch, you gain a bonus on that check equal to a roll of your Bardic Inspiration die. This roll doesn't expend the die.

sheet.description: Whenever you make an Intelligence check relating to the cosmos or the eldritch, add 1d{{bardic-inspiration:dice}} to the check without expending a Bardic Inspiration die.

element.name: Level 6: Devouring Maw
element.source: Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: Your words can call beings from beyond the veil. When a creature that possesses a Bardic Inspiration die from you is targeted by an attack, it can take a Reaction to expend the die, summoning an eldritch maw that engulfs and protects it. The target gains Resistance to the triggering damage and is ripped through space by the maw, teleporting it to a point within 5 feet of you. This Reaction fails if you have the Incapacitated or Unconscious condition or if you are further than 90 feet from the target.

sheet.description: A creature with your Bardic Inspiration die targeted by an attack can use its Reaction to expend the die, gaining Resistance to the triggering damage and teleporting to within 5 ft of you (fails if you are Incapacitated, Unconscious, or >90 ft away).

element.name: Level 14: Song of the Apocalypse
element.source: Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: You always have the Divine Order: Transcend spell prepared. You can cast the spell once without expending a spell slot, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest.

In addition, when you cast the spell with this feature, or when you use an Eldritch Melody that requires Concentration, the apocalypse flows through you; damage can't break your Concentration on this spell or the melody, and you automatically succeed on the saving throws to keep control over the spell.

sheet.description: You can cast Divine Order: Transcend once without a spell slot. When cast this way, or when using a Concentration Eldritch Melody, damage can't break your Concentration and you auto-succeed on saves to keep control over the spell.

element.name: Ballad of the Nameless City
element.source: Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: You channel the name of the lost city of the Great Ones, warping reality. Each creature in a 30-foot Emanation originating from you must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed up to 10 feet in a direction of your choice and have the Prone condition.
The maximum distance a creature is pushed on failed save increases when you reach Bard levels 6 (20 feet) and 14 (30 feet).

sheet.description: Each creature in a 30-ft Emanation makes a DC{{bard:spellcasting:dc}} Str save or is pushed up to {{ballad nameless city:push}} ft in a direction of your choice and falls Prone.

element.name: Concord of the Depths
element.source: Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: You sing a hypnotic melody that evokes the presence of the sleeping horrors beneath the waves. One creature of your choice within 60 feet of yourself must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target has the Incapacitated condition and its Speed is reduced to 0. These effects last for 1 minute, until the target takes damage, or until a creature uses an action to shake or slap the target out of its stupor.

Starting at Bard level 6, the number of creatures you can choose to make the saving throw when you use this feature increases to two creatures. At Bard level 14, it increases to a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of three).

sheet.description: {{concord of the depths:targets}} creature(s) within 60 ft make a DC{{bard:spellcasting:dc}} Wis save or are Incapacitated with Speed 0 for 1 min (ends if damaged or shaken awake with an action).

element.name: Epode of the Crimson Toll
element.source: Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: You toll the bells of death, beckoning bloodshed in a 30-foot Emanation originating from you until the end of your next turn. You and any allies in the Emanation have a bonus to attack rolls equal to half your Charisma modifier (rounded up). For the next minute, you can take a Bonus Action on later turns to keep tolling the bells, maintaining the effect until the end of your next turn each time you do so. Deafened creatures gain no benefit from this melody.
Starting at Bard level 6, the bonus also applies to damage rolls with attacks. At Bard level 14, the bonus to damage rolls becomes equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1).

sheet.alt: Epode of the Crimson Toll (Melody, Conc.)
sheet.description: 30-ft Emanation until end of next turn (Bonus Action to extend up to 1 min; Deafened creatures gain no benefit): You and allies gain +{{charisma:modifier:half:up}} to attack rolls.
30-ft Emanation until end of next turn (Bonus Action to extend up to 1 min; Deafened creatures gain no benefit): You and allies gain +{{charisma:modifier:half:up}} to attack and damage rolls.

30-ft Emanation until end of next turn (Bonus Action to extend up to 1 min; Deafened creatures gain no benefit): You and allies gain +{{charisma:modifier:half:up}} to attack rolls and +{{epode:damage}} to damage rolls.

element.name: Prelude of the Inevitable
element.source: Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: You announce the turn of fate, and the chosen answers the call. You touch one willing creature. For the next hour, the target can add a number to its Initiative rolls equal to one roll of your Bardic Inspiration.

Starting at Bard level 6, you can affect two willing creatures when you use this melody. At Bard level 14, you can affect a number of willing creatures equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of three).

sheet.description: Touch {{prelude inevitable:targets}} willing creature(s). For 1 hr, targets add 1d{{bardic-inspiration:dice}} to their Initiative rolls.

element.name: Transcendence of Flesh
element.source: Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: You sing a gloria in the name of corruption, calling forth writhing, protective tentacles that sprout from the mouths, eyes, and ears of your allies. Each willing creature of your choice in a 30-foot Emanation originating from you gains Temporary Hit Points equal to half your Bard level + your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1 Temporary Hit Point). While a creature has these Temporary Hit Points, it has Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.

sheet.description: Willing creatures of your choice in a 30-ft Emanation gain {{transcendence of flesh:thp}} THP. While having these THP, they have Advantage on Str checks and Str saves.

element.name: Aria of the Reviled Stalker
element.source: Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: You sing a haunting melody that evokes the presence of the lurking horrors beyond the veil. Choose one willing creature within 30 feet of you. For 1 hour, it is partially absorbed by the cosmos. For the duration, the target has a +10 bonus to Stealth checks, and it can't be tracked except by magical means. In addition, as an action, the target can become incorporeal and move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain until the end of its turn. If it ends its turn inside an object, it takes 5 (1d10) Force damage and is immediately shunted to the nearest unoccupied space. Once the creature takes this action, it can't do so again for the duration of the transformation.
Starting at Bard level 14, when the creature takes an action to become incorporeal, the effect lasts for 10 minutes instead.

sheet.alt: Aria of the Reviled Stalker (Melody, Conc.)
sheet.description: 1 willing creature within 30 ft gains +10 to Stealth and can't be tracked nonmagically for 1 hr. Once during the duration, it can use an action to become incorporeal until the end of its turn (10 mins at level 14), moving through creatures/objects as Difficult Terrain (5 [1d10] Force damage and shunted if ending turn inside an object).

element.name: Ode to Subjugation
element.source: Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: You invoke the power of a devouring Great One, summoning forth a horde of writhing tentacles to ensnare your enemies. Each creature of your choice that you can see in a 20-foot Emanation centered on you must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or become Restrained for 1 minute. A Restrained creature repeats the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
Starting at Bard level 14, a Restrained creature takes 3d6 Necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns.

sheet.description: Chosen creatures in a 20-ft Emanation make a DC{{bard:spellcasting:dc}} Dex save or are Restrained for 1 min (save ends at end of turns).

Chosen creatures in a 20-ft Emanation make a DC{{bard:spellcasting:dc}} Dex save or are Restrained for 1 min (save ends at end of turns). Restrained creatures take 3d6 Necrotic damage at the start of each of their turns.

element.name: Requiem of Chaos
element.source: Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: You don the visage of the Crawling Chaos, whispering your enemies' demise. Choose one creature within 60 feet of you. It has Disadvantage on Wisdom checks and Wisdom saving throws until the end of your next turn. This Disadvantage applies even if the creature would have Advantage from other sources.
Starting at Bard level 14, you can target two creatures.

sheet.description: Choose {{requiem of chaos:targets}} creature(s) within 60 ft. It has Disadvantage on Wis checks and saves until the end of your next turn (overrides Advantage).

element.name: Song of Abject Birth
element.source: Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: You invoke the power of the primordial chaos, hurling forth a horde of writhing fetuses. Each creature in a 30-foot Cone must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking a number of d4s of Necrotic damage equal to your Bard level on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.
Starting at Bard level 14, the Cone's size increases to 60 feet.

sheet.description: Each creature in a {{song abject birth:cone}}-ft Cone makes a DC{{bard:spellcasting:dc}} Dex save or takes {{level:bard}}d4 Necrotic damage (half on success).

element.name: Assonance of Dreams
element.source: Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: You sing a melody that allows travel through the dream realm. You conjure a circular portal up to 20 feet in diameter that links an unoccupied space you can see within 10 feet of yourself with a precise location you are very familiar with within 1 mile of yourself on the same plane of existence as you. You can orient the portal in any direction you choose. The portal lasts for 1 minute.
Anything that travels through the portal is instantly transported to the location you chose, appearing in an unoccupied space nearest to the location.

sheet.description: Conjure a 20-ft diameter portal within 10 ft linking to a very familiar location within 1 mile on the same plane for 1 min. Anything passing through teleports to the nearest unoccupied space at the destination.

element.name: Euphony of Revelations
element.source: Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: You carve the ancient symbol of the convergence of light, creating a portal to realms untold. Choose a point you can see within 60 feet of yourself. Each creature in a 5-foot Emanation originating from that point must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be drawn through the portal to an unknown destination. At the end of your next turn, the targets return to the spaces they previously occupied, or the nearest unoccupied space. If a target isn't an Aberration, it takes 5d12 Psychic damage and must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or gain a Long-Term Madness.

sheet.description: Choose a point within 60 ft. Creatures in a 5-ft Emanation make a DC{{bard:spellcasting:dc}} Cha save or are drawn through a portal until the end of your next turn. Upon return, non-Aberrations take 5d12 Psychic damage and make a DC{{bard:spellcasting:dc}} Wis save or gain Long-Term Madness.

element.name: Nightmare of the Abyss
element.source: Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: You recite the forbidden incantations of He Who Lies Dreaming, summoning forth a vision of the being's power. Five creatures of your choice within 60 feet of you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the Stunned condition until the end of your next turn.

sheet.description: 5 chosen creatures within 60 ft make a DC{{bard:spellcasting:dc}} Wis save or are Stunned until the end of your next turn.

element.name: Whispers of the Flesh-Defiler
element.source: Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: You recite forbidden lore learned from a tome of flesh, summoning a swarm of buzzing, entrail-eating worms in a 30-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point you can see within 60 feet of yourself. The Sphere lasts for 1 minute.

When the Sphere appears, each creature in it is devoured by the worms and must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes 8d6 Necrotic damage and has the Poisoned condition for 1 minute. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only. A creature also makes this save when the spell's area moves into its space and when it enters the spell's area or ends its turn there. A creature makes this save only once per turn. A Poisoned creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
On each of your turns after you summon the swarm, you can take a Bonus Action to move it up to 30 feet in any direction. This melody ends early if you take Fire or Radiant damage.

sheet.description: 30-ft Sphere within 60 ft for 1 min (Bonus Action to move 30 ft; ends early if you take Fire or Radiant damage). Creatures inside on cast, when area moves onto them, entering, or ending turn make a DC{{bard:spellcasting:dc}} Con save (1/turn) or take 8d6 Necrotic damage and become Poisoned 1 min (half dmg on success; save ends at end of turns).
